title: The Probability Ranking Principle: Visual Guide
outline: Title: The Probability Ranking Principle: Visual Guide

1. Sorting By Probability | four candidate documents at P(R=1) = 0.9, 0.7, 0.4, 0.2 that the learner reorders, with expected precision@k recomputed at every cutoff | one descending sort maximises expected precision@k and recall@k at all cutoffs simultaneously, by linearity of expectation, and any swap gives expected relevant results away for nothing

2. Rank Or Threshold | sliders for the false-positive and false-negative costs driving the Bayes-optimal cutoff C_fp/(C_fp+C_fn), plus a toggle from probability to log-odds | monotone transforms and dropped constants preserve the ranking but destroy the cutoff, so thresholding a retrieved set needs calibration that a rank-only score never promised

3. Deriving The RSV | a six-step tap-through from the posterior to RSV(d), showing the expression at each stage and the assumption that bought the step | odds plus Bayes cancels the normaliser, dropping the prior odds is free for ranking, independence factors across terms, and the multiply-and-divide trick removes the absent-term product, leaving a sum of per-term weights an inverted index can walk

4. The RSJ Weight | a live 2x2 contingency table over n_t, R and r_t with the +0.5 correction, computing c_t and its two log-odds halves, with worked-example and no-judgment presets | the RSJ weight is the difference between how strongly relevant and non-relevant documents attract a term, the +0.5 in every cell stops a zero cell producing an infinite weight, and R = 0 collapses the relevant side to 1

5. Where idf Comes From | the RSJ zero-knowledge weight and the classic ln(N/n_t) plotted together against document frequency from 1 to 100,000, with the n_t > N/2 region shaded | idf is not a separate heuristic but the no-knowledge limit of the RSJ weight, the two variants agree closely for rare terms, and the RSJ form goes negative once a term appears in more than half the collection
